summary: Comprehensive backend + frontend testing of magic-login 'resume your setup' feature (POST /auth/magic-login/exchange & /refresh, /magic-login React route). 10/10 backend pytest cases pass, 5/5 frontend Playwright scenarios pass. Covers valid exchange for both stages, single-use replay (410), bogus token (404), expired-unused (410), refresh mint+consume flow, refresh replay dead, click tracking increment, dry-run preview not minting real tokens, bare /magic-login dead state, and GitHub wizard auto-open on landing (Step 1/3, 'Continue with GitHub App' primary + RECOMMENDED, PAT collapsed as secondary — external GitHub auth NOT bypassed).

minor.issue: Both 'already_used' and 'expired' return HTTP 410 with different detail strings ('already_used' vs 'expired'), but frontend (MagicLogin.jsx) branches only on status code — so a REPLAYED (already-used) valid token shows the same 'This link has expired' UI as a genuinely expired one. Not silent (spec-compliant), but message is misleading. Consider distinct 4xx codes (e.g., 409 for used vs 410 for expired) OR have frontend parse response.detail.

integration_issues.issue: Replayed just-used token shows 'This link has expired' + 'get a new one' button. Clicking it correctly fails (backend 410 already_used → refresh) and falls to dead UI, so no silent auth — but the two-step user experience is confusing. See backend minor issue above.

action_items: OPTIONAL/MINOR: differentiate 'already_used' vs 'expired' at the frontend so a replayed used token shows the true 'This link isn't valid — it may have already been used' dead state directly (currently shows 'expired' → 'get a new one' fails → then dead).
critical_code_review_comments: backend/routers/auth.py:670-693 — /magic-login/refresh will happily mint+consume a new token for ANY unused row, including one whose expires_at is still in the future. That's technically fine (possession of the original 32-byte opaque token is inbox-proof) but is slightly inconsistent with the docstring 'only for a token that's genuinely just time-expired'. Consider gating refresh with `if old_row.get('expires_at', 0) > time.time(): raise 400` if the founder wants refresh to be strictly for expired links only. Currently non-blocking.
frontend/src/pages/MagicLogin.jsx:66 — status===410 collapses both already_used and expired into 'expired' UI. See minor bug above.
test_credentials: Created TEST_ prefixed dev_users + magic_login_tokens rows on-the-fly inside the tests, cleaned up in fixture teardown. Founder preview creds NOT needed.
seed_data_creation: test_magic_login_2026_08_20.py inserts+deletes TEST_ prefixed rows in db=aurem_dev, collections: dev_users, magic_login_tokens, onboarding_emails. Verified full cleanup — 0 TEST_ rows remain after run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: backend test file at /app/backend/tests/test_magic_login_2026_08_20.py is idempotent — safe to re-run any time. Uses REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL from env, MONGO_URL default localhost. It relies on the funnel_nudge_cron.magic_click_url signature (preview kwarg) — if the cron signature changes, TestDryRunNudge will need updating.
rca of the issue: No blocking issues. One minor UX quirk documented: frontend cannot distinguish already-used vs expired since backend uses HTTP 410 for both. Spec-compliant (no silent auto-login on replay) but message wording is not ideal for the replay path. Recommend: check response body detail string in MagicLogin.jsx, or have backend return 409 for already_used.
